description.narrative:
The aim of project is to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of interisland shipping services through provision of an integrated package of assistance. It comprises two major components:
(a) infrastructure investments in the capital of Port Vila and five outer islands, and
(b) establishment of a shipping support scheme to catalyze the provision of services to remote noncommercial destinations using an output-based aid approach.
The Project is complemented by associated TA to improve sector governance through institutional strengthening and legal and regulatory reforms, and by project management services.

Progress Toward Outcome: As of 21 April 2025, the civil works at South Paray, Lenakel, and Litzlitz were largely completed.
Under the shipping support scheme, five routes were identified with 194.5 voyages completed as of 15 Oct 2024.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Jun 2023: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/42392/42392-013-apfs-en_4.pdf
Some results are in the Environmental and Social Monitoring Reports | Mar 2025: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/42392/42392-013-esmr-en_14.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: Output 1 is complete as of 21 April 2025. Redesigning of all five wharves under the project was already completed (South Paray, Simonsen, Port Sandwich, Lenakel, and Litzlitz). Designs were verified by independent international design reviewer firm. Lenakel and Litzlitz wharves contract was awarded on 26 July 2021 and repair works completed in June and July 2022, respectively. South Paray wharf contract was awarded on 16 June 2022 and the civil works was completed on 16 April 2025. Package for Port Sandwich and Simonsen is no longer pushing through under this project due to the financing gap.
Output 2 was completed as of Q4 2024. Shipping services covered Tafea East, Tafea West, Torres, Santo, and Banks under the SSS component. All contracts were awarded by July 2021 and these shipping services became operational. However, in February 2022, Santo route contract was terminated by the government. Shipping coordinators were replaced by shipping administrator scheme where the Ministry of Infrastructure and Public Utilities have established its own shipping services unit to administer the scheme. Shipping Administrator and Shipping Support Unit are undertaking the tasks. Shipping administrators (replacing shipping coordinators) exceeded the target of 25% women participation (2 out of 2, 100%).
Output 3 is completed considering the completion of project's shipping support scheme component by Q4 2024 and the completion of civil works of South Paray wharf. 57% of national staff in PIU are women. (4 women out of a total of 7 staff members in the PIU).
Output 4 was completed with Maritime Safety Regulator Bill passed by the Parliament in December 2016 and funds were included in government budget.
